@Ronway, this is exactly why I said I could see this ruling going either way and I would not be surprised. Both interpretations make sense to me oddly enough.

I think the issue at play here is the inherent differences in a Character card and a non-Character target.

Sticking with the Operative for a moment, allow me to make my case another way. The Chairman has a two cards in his deck that causes both the Chairman and Operative to either do direct damage or heal, and the wording on these cards is interesting. Basically the wording on these cards is "The Chairman does X. If the Operative is Active, she does X"

The intent of these cards is for a secondary action to occure if the Operative has not flipped. This leads me to think that Character cards have two states, "Active" and "Incapacitated" (Non-Active). I think these two states of "being" are inherently different from the states of being that non-Character targets can have, that of being "In Play" and "Leaving Play" (the Destroy mechanic). For a target to "leave play", in my interpretation, it must be "Destroyed" (Tempest and Into the Strata being the exception).

A Character card, as we know, can not be destroyed, therefore follows it can not leave play. Or we can reword that last sentence. A Character card goes from being an "Active" target to an "Incapacitated" target (non-active). The Character card does not cese to be "target" in this sense, but just ceses to be an "active" target. But the Operative is still in the play area and still impacts the game mechanically, something a target that is "not in play" can not do.

That was rather long for an interpretation that I am not married to haha

About the Jack Handle/Dual Crowbars with Bloody Knuckles/Hunter and Hunted thing:  I spent two days thinking long and hard about it, arrived a conclusion which contradicted Spiff's Rules and Clarifications, wrote 1500 words attempting to justify why I thought doubling up on buffs was a better interpretation of the text on the cards than dealing static damage (ignoring Voss' armour makes me feel really uncomfortable) and then read this post: https://greaterthangames.com/comment/3949#comment-3949 which put me straight on that matter.  To get over avoiding soak I'm going to start playing with the house rule that Jack Handle reads:

“Whenever Mr Fixer would deal damage to a target, he instead directs that damage to, and finishes the damage calculation for, all non-hero targets.  Whenever this card enters play, return any other tool cards in play to your hand.”

Meaning if (x+b-c) is the damage I would deal to a target, Jack Handle means I’d deal each non-hero (x+b-c)-d.  Where x is the basic damage of an “attack”, b is the increase to damage afforded by buffs, c is the damage reduction on the “original” target and d is the damage reduction on each subsequent target.  You're double-dipping the soak, but if that's an issue maybe you should play Alternating Tiger Claw ;)

An official ruling on both of them would be nice.

No, just entering play doesn't make something a target.  Ground Pound isn't a target just because it was played.  My logic goes like this:

  • I play Razor Ordanance.  It's put into play in front of me.  It is not a target.  I have no targets in play.
  • Next, the Realm of Discord turns it into a target.  There were no targets in front of me before this event, but there are now.  The target must have entered play since it wasn't there before (if it didn't enter play, how'd it get there?).  The card was there before, but the target wasn't.

Regardless of that, this is how I would rule the situation:

I am the player controlling Haka and keeping count of other cards are of no interest to me:

  1. Start of the game.  I have 0 cards in play, I have 0 targets in play.
  2. I play Ground Pound. I have 1 card in play, I have 0 targets in play.  Ground Pound has entered play, so I trigger its effect.
  3. Imbued Vitality enters play.  Ground Pound becomes a target.  I have 1 card in play. I have 1 target in play.  Compared to the previous stage, Ground Pound has gained the quality of being a target.  One target has entered play but no more cards have entered play.  I would not reactivate ground pound.
  4. A bounty is attached to Ground Pound, as it is a target.  I have 1 card in play, I have 1 target in play.
  5. Imbued Vitality leaves play.  Ground Pound loses the property of being a target.  I have 1 card in play.  I have 0 targets in play.  Compared to the previous stage, a target has left play.  That target is Ground Pound.  The bounty is destroyed because Ground Pound (the target) has left play, even though Ground Pound (the card) is still in play.
  6. I destroy Ground Pound.  I have 0 cards in play, I have 0 targets in play.
This has helped me decide on my stance with Bounties vs The Ennead, thanks everyone!
